en.title: Rome I, Irish version: is a large-risk insurance contract without a choice governed by the law of the consumer or of the insurer?
en.summary: The other versions point to the law of the country where the insurer has his habitual residence. The Irish text names the consumer, a party that a large-risk insurance contract does not have.
en.impact: For a large-risk policy between an insurer in one Member State and a business policy holder in another, without a choice of law, the Irish text points away from the insurer's country.
en.correction: The lawyer-linguists could say whether the wording should be aligned with the other versions: replace the consumer with the insurer in Irish Article 7(2), second subparagraph.

quote_translations.q1: the law of the country where the consumer has his habitual residence

ga.title: An Róimh I, an leagan Gaeilge: an é dlí an tomhaltóra nó dlí an árachóra a rialaíonn conradh árachais a chumhdaíonn mór-riosca nuair nach ndearnadh rogha dlí?
ga.summary: Díríonn na leaganacha eile ar dhlí na tíre ina bhfuil gnáthchónaí ar an árachóir. Ainmníonn an téacs Gaeilge an tomhaltóir, páirtí nach bhfuil i gconradh árachais a chumhdaíonn mór-riosca.
ga.impact: I gcás polasaí a chumhdaíonn mór-riosca idir árachóir i mBallstát amháin agus sealbhóir polasaí ar gnólacht é i mBallstát eile, gan rogha dlí, díríonn an téacs Gaeilge ar dhlí nach é dlí thír an árachóra é.
ga.correction: D'fhéadfadh na dlítheangeolaithe a rá ar cheart an fhoclaíocht a ailíniú leis na leaganacha eile: an t-árachóir a chur in ionad an tomhaltóra sa dara fomhír de mhír 2 d'Airteagal 7 den leagan Gaeilge.
